---
title: Start to Search
---

## Overview

A SearchAgent run loads questions, builds one agent per task, calls tools until the
model produces a final response or reaches a configured limit, and writes each full
trajectory to disk.

## Prerequisites

You need an LLM endpoint compatible with the selected client and parser. You also need
at least one retrieval source:

- **Local files:** install `ripgrep` and point a `file` source at a directory.
- **Elasticsearch:** start Elasticsearch `<9.0.0`, create an index, and install the
  optional dependency with `uv sync --extra elasticsearch-source`.
- **Embedding retrieval:** populate the index's vector field and provide an
  OpenAI-compatible embedding endpoint.

Install the optional terminal UI dependency for demo with TUI

```bash
uv sync --extra tui
```

Use `searchagent plugins deploy local-wiki --help` or
`searchagent plugins deploy browsecomp-plus --help` for the bundled indexing flows.

## Configure the agent

Start from `src/searchagent/config/config.yaml` or one of the packaged model configs:

| Config | Parser | Tool interface |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `webexplorer.yaml` | `upstream` | Batched `search(queries)` and `browse(url, query)` |
| `websailor.yaml` | `websailor` | Batched `search(query)` and `visit(url, goal)` |
| `tongyi_deepresearch.yaml` | `tongyi_deep_research` | Batched `search(query)` and `visit(url, goal)` |

These files contain deployment-specific model paths, endpoints, index names, and high
concurrency defaults. Copy one and replace those values for your environment or use hydra-style command-line overrides. The essential fields are the client, parser, sources,
tools, data, and output directory.

```yaml
agent:
  llm_client:
    type: openai
    model: Qwen3-8B
    openai:
      api_key: EMPTY
      base_url: http://127.0.0.1:8001/v1
  parser:
    type: upstream
  sources:
    - type: file
      name: docs
      root_path: ./docs
  tools:
    - type: search
      name: search
      source: [docs]
    - type: visit
      name: visit
      source: [docs]
  system_prompt: >-
    Use the tools to verify the answer. Put the final answer in
    <answer></answer> tags.
  max_turn: 20
  max_tokens: 32768

dataloader:
  source: data/questions.jsonl
  input_key: question
  answer_key: answer

max_concurrency: 16
output_path: outputs/demo
```

`max_turn`, `max_tokens`, and optional timeout settings bound each trajectory. Their
corresponding reminder prompts ask the model to stop using tools and produce a final
answer near the limit.

## Validate

Inspect the composed config before starting expensive inference:

```bash
searchagent inspect --config-name config
```

Use Hydra-style overrides for environment-specific values:

```bash
searchagent run --config-name webexplorer \
  agent.llm_client.model=WebExplorer-8B \
  agent.llm_client.openai.base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8001/v1 \
  agent.sources.0.hosts=http://127.0.0.1:9200 \
  dataloader.source=data/questions.jsonl \
  output_path=outputs/webexplorer
```

Packaged configs are resolved from `src/searchagent/config`. For a config elsewhere,
pass its directory with `--config-path` and its filename without `.yaml` with
`--config-name`.

## Logging

```yaml
logging:
  global_file: ${output_path}/run.log
  trace:
    enabled: true
    dir: ${output_path}/traces
    format: text
    level: DEBUG
    filename_template: "{sample_id}_{trace_id}.log"
```

The global log shows batch progress and failures. Per-trace logs isolate model and tool
events for one sample, which is usually the fastest way to diagnose a bad trajectory.

## Interactive TUI

Launch the TUI to watch the run in real time, inspect traces, and replay a sample with

```bash
searchagent tui --config-name webexplorer
searchagent tui --config-name websailor
```
